# Personal learning review: worked definition exercise

**Illustrative thought experiment.** The people, requirements, configurations, weeks, records and results below are stipulated for testing the draft. They are not observations of the owner's life, Dream or an implemented service. This is an independent personal case. Local labels identify parts of this example only.

Read with [process](../standard/ontology/concepts/process.md), [system and implementation](../standard/ontology/concepts/system.md), [requirements](../standard/ontology/concepts/requirement.md), and [assessment](../standard/assessment/requirement-and-need-fulfillment.md).

## Need, requirements and contribution

The learner wants useful understanding of three selected concepts to remain available when doing related work, without consuming the time reserved for other responsibilities.

The example's learner chooses these requirements, revision A:

| Label | Statement and criterion | Required conditions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | By Sunday 20:00 local time, the weekly sheet contains an explanation for each of the three selected concepts. Each explanation must correctly state the concept, give a correct worked example and counterexample, and cite an available supporting reference. The learner judges each against the selected reference and records the reason. All three must satisfy all four checks. | A week with three concepts selected in advance and a suitable source pack available locally before work begins. Work must be supported both when connected and when a session has no network access. |
| P2 | Total time spent preparing, studying, drafting and reviewing the sheet is at most 120 minutes that week. | Same week and scope as P1; time includes rework, not only reading. |

The purpose of P1 is to make understanding retrievable and expose misunderstandings; P2 protects competing responsibilities. The causal assumption is that producing and checking these explanations improves later application. Neither a completed sheet nor an accepted explanation proves that assumption. The learner's longer-term judgment of usefulness concerns the need, not an extra unstated condition of P1.

P1 is high-level relative to detailed retrieval, drafting and checking requirements. It remains high-level for this arrangement after work is allocated to those activities. The chosen counts and deadlines are this example's criteria, not universal provisions of the standard.

## System, structure and implementation

The boundary includes the learner, a local source pack, a weekly sheet, a timer, study activities and review decisions. The reference publisher is an external dependency. Later work that might benefit from the learning is outside the sheet-production process but relevant to need fulfillment.

The structure connects three explanation entries to their references and review reasons. The process selects the concepts, prepares local references, studies, drafts, checks and either revises or closes the weekly attempt. Neither a folder of references nor a timer alone produces the combined result.

Configuration A is a hypothetical implementation consisting of local reference files, a sheet template, a timer and the learner's review routine. It exists in the scenario even if a template link is broken or an explanation is wrong. Its implementation status does not establish readiness, accuracy or useful learning.

## Description, responsibility and progression

The intended description requires failed checks to be resolved before successful completion, while allowing the deadline to end an unsuccessful attempt. The stipulated existing practice in Week A is to end the attempt at the deadline with one correction outstanding. This is deadline-based stopping, not successful completion. Describing this practice does not authorize it as compliant.

The learner maintains the routine, performs the work, answers for unresolved corrections, chooses future process changes and judges the sheet. These responsibilities are distinguishable even though one person holds all of them. Finishing this week's attempt does not end responsibility for next week's preparation or an outstanding correction. Retaining a flawed sheet as a working copy does not change P1.

| State subject | Event or decision and condition | Result and responsible response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Weekly execution | Weekly start; concepts selected and source pack prepared | Ready; learner starts work. Missing references instead block preparation. |
| Weekly execution | Learner starts with inputs available | Studying, then drafting; learner produces the entries. |
| Explanation entry | Draft submitted to the four checks | Reviewed; a failed check requires correction owned by the learner. |
| Weekly execution | Deadline reached; learner closes this attempt with correction outstanding | Attempt ended with an open correction. Closure is not fulfillment. |

These are example-specific states. An explanation's review state is separate from the execution state and the requirement assessment. A network outage is an external event, not an approval decision; the learner responds using the prepared local pack or records a blocked activity if it is unusable.

## Week A: stipulated occurrence and records

The examined scope is one connected week using Configuration A and requirement revision A. Three entries were produced by the deadline. The stipulated sheet review records that A and B pass all checks; C has an incorrect counterexample. The stipulated complete time record totals 95 minutes. These records are invented inputs to this reasoning exercise, not empirical evidence.

The learner assesses the week just after the Sunday deadline:

| Question | Bounded conclusion |
| --- | --- |
| Did the activity finish and produce its output? | The attempt ended and the sheet was produced. The correction remains outstanding. |
| Was P1 satisfied for this week? | No. Two of three entries satisfy its checks; the requirement demands all three. Report partial achievement alongside an unmet criterion, without replacing both with an unexplained grade. |
| Was P2 satisfied for this week? | Yes, given the stipulated complete record: 95 minutes is within 120. |
| What about offline operation? | Not examined. Its coverage and performance are unknown; retain it in the required conditions. |
| Is this reliable over time? | Unknown. One hypothetical week cannot establish a repeated success rate or future capability. |
| Was the result accepted? | The learner retains the sheet with an explicit correction outstanding. This decision does not make P1 satisfied. |
| Was the need met? | Not established. The sheet and time record do not show whether understanding remains available or useful during later work. |

The 2/3 count describes entries passing the quality checks in this week. It is not a measured probability of success, proof of supported capability, or percentage of the underlying need met. Missing records of later use mean unknown benefit, not evidence that no later use happened.

## Counterexamples, costs and review

Even if all three explanations pass, the learner might be unable to apply them later. That counterexample challenges the adequacy of the selected requirements for the need. Conversely, spending 170 minutes correcting the sheet could satisfy P1 and fail P2; an improvement in one result can undermine another requirement.

Reassess relevant conclusions if the concepts, references, rubric, time allowance, process or implementation changes. Do not transfer this week's judgment to a new configuration automatically.

The exercise shows that the repaired definitions can distinguish existing and intended practice, a defective implementation, and a requirement's relative level. It exposes unresolved choices about how to summarize partial achievement alongside an unmet all-cases criterion and which facts must always be recorded. It does not establish that the candidate schema is minimal or that independent authors will interpret it consistently.
